Tracheids and vessel elements are two types of xylem cells that provide support and conduct water and minerals in plants. They are dead, hollow cells with thick, rigid cell walls, found in the xylem tissue, that allow for the transport of water and minerals.

subject: college_biology
text: Tracheids and vessel elements are two types of xylem cells that provide support and conduct water and minerals in plants. They are responsible for transporting water and minerals from the roots to the leaves. Tracheids are dead cells with a single opening, while vessel elements are connected to form vessels for water transport.

text: The neritic zone is a marine ecosystem region characterized by penetrance of solar radiation and upwelling of nutrients, supporting an abundance of marine life. It is also known as the sublittoral zone. This area is located between the shoreline and the continental shelf.
